title: Guard refusals stricter than their rule are narrowed to the rule's outcome
why: Follow-ups from the refusal-versus-rule sweep (step refusal-matches-rule; owner Nov 1 20:57 CST).
note: Items: command-in-item (any semicolon or pipe in a code span counts as a shell line); gh-login-switch (a str_replace that keeps the switch is refused); machine-wide-kill (lsof -ti list and pkill -P <own pid> refused); detached-launch (foreground nohup or setsid -w refused); impeccable-review-only (a semicolon in Skill args refused); builder-test-edit (scratchpad and docs/spec paths counted as tests); records-page (refused even when the page is unchanged); destructive-delete (a cat heredoc whose text names a delete is refused); merge preview-base-run (says --confirm refuses it, though --base-red-ok lifts it); the merge tool's "No override lifts this refusal" line, false for red-base and dropped-lane. Batch clause: step overlapping-batches; it reaches the guard's merge-checks rule through Host.head_read and needs a guard test there. Ready. Source: lane refusal-matches-rule, draft PR #1029, record docs/plans/refusal-vs-rule.md section "Follow-up steps", Nov 1 21:11 CST. Each item is one fix with its own red-first case; a lane may take any subset. Port: yes, the guards are shared. Added (Nov 1 21:15 CST): press-link: the check asks for a link on an option the session presses after the owner's pick (for example "Merge PR #374"); it must judge only presses the owner makes. Lane started Nov 1 21:15 CST. Lane split into 3 PRs by file (Nov 1 21:25 CST): guard.py items; question_form.py items (command-in-item, gh-login-switch, press-link); merge.py text. The batch-clause guard test is in step overlapping-batches. Added (Nov 1 21:18 CST, PR #1029 head 9fe8c7bd): pointer-head is stricter than decision recovery-independent-of-state: git switch -C main origin/main is refused though HEAD stays on main. Added (Nov 1 21:40 CST, lane test-practices-first-principles, PR #1028 head 831d758db): lint check_ruling_kind and the prose judge conflict. The judge requires a Kind: process line under a new section of a decision; the lint fails on two Kind lines; the judge refuses both ways out. One of the two must yield: one Kind line per record (rule git-one-record-per-question) means a section with its own kind is its own record. Notes line check-ruling-kind-judge-conflict. Lane notes, Nov 1 21:45 CST: records-page leaves this step: its refusal is exact for what the guard can see (it runs before the generator), so the PR #1029 row should read exact, limit accepted. destructive-delete heredoc row is stale: main already allows a quoted text heredoc that names a delete. impeccable: only a review verb after a semicolon passes; audit; polish stays refused. One line still owed here: decision records-index-at-merge names the records-page limit (the guard runs before the generator, so it cannot tell whether a commit changes the page). PR #1029 head 45bb774b counts: exact 87, stricter 11, looser 9, uncited 32, unverified 1. Kind-line conflict fix: draft PR #1043, head 85dc7944, with batch runner 7 (lane, Nov 1 22:24 CST). PR #1028 adds note check-ruling-kind-judge-conflict, which goes stale when #1043 merges. Once both merge, remove that note line; this lane takes it if still open, else it stays on this step. Lane correction, Nov 1 22:55 CST: the destructive-delete looser row is live (`rm -r $(pwd)/*` passes on main, `rm -r ./*` is refused); only the stricter heredoc part was stale; PR #1039 (step refusal-looser-fixes) covers the $(pwd)/* form. This lane closes `nohup setsid -f` in round 2. Note: builder-test repo_rel uses normpath, not realpath, so a symlink from outside a repo into its test folder passes (low odds). Nov 2 00:03 CST: every item is in a draft PR with batch runner 7: #1043 (Kind-line conflict), #1047 (merge tool text), #1050 (question-form items), #1060 (guard items: kill, detached, pointer-head, builder-test, impeccable). records-page is exact, its limit accepted and written into records-index-at-merge (#1060). destructive-delete has no stricter part left.
